Senses.Explanation: To appraise, sort out, or distinguish; noun constructions name the resulting appraisal or classificatory distinction. The term is attested 266 times in 126 allowlisted texts. Nanyue Jiqi Hongchu's unnamed questioner sets two episodes side by side and asks Nanyue to “please appraise and distinguish” them (兩段不同，試請料揀); Wuyi Yuanlai asks who can sort out a presented conjunction. The same appraisal vocabulary appears in Linji's “Four Selections” (四料揀). The Eye of Humans and Gods records Nanyuan Huiyong asking Fengxue Yanzhao, “the Four Selections—what do the selections select?” (四料揀，料揀何法), and compiler Huiyan Zhizhao begins another exposition with people of middle and lower capacity under that heading. Zhanran Yuancheng calls paired evaluative formulas “the old so-called selection sayings” (古所謂料揀語). The public act, resulting distinction, and named set remain one appraisal-and-selection family; noun and verb grammar alone do not create different lexical things.
Senses.Note: The former action/result targets were not independently distinguishable from their glosses. The standalone word remains compatible with the separate named Four Selections article and its four formulations. The Chan deviation is public appraisal of sayings, encounters, and speakers, plus its use in Linji classificatory vocabulary.
